### Body
I’m curious how other developers here use GitHub when applying for jobs.
Some companies check your GitHub profile before or after interviews, so I’m wondering:
What kind of projects do you keep public for employers to see?
Do you write detailed READMEs to explain your work?
How much do recruiters actually value GitHub contributions compared to a traditional resume? | 1You must be logged in to vote All reactions Answered by [Banabanaa](https://github.com/Banabanaa)[on Aug 14, 2025Aug 14, 2025](https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/169760#discussioncomment-14099179) I try to put effort into writing good README files — I treat them almost like a portfolio write-up. I include: - What the project is - What tools/technologies were used - Setup instructions - Screenshots or demo links - A brief explanation of what I learned or solved As for how much GitHub matters compared to a resume: It really depends on the company. Tech-first or open source-friendly companies often take GitHub seriously — sometimes more than a resume. But for more traditional companies, it's just a bonus. Either way, a well-curated GitHub profile can absolutely help you stand out and back up your skills with real work. # What You Need for a Great Developer Website, GitHub, and LinkedIn

## Your LinkedIn profile, your GitHub portfolio, and your personal developer site all support your resume. Here’s how to stand out.

(Photo by [Nagara Oyodo](https://unsplash.com/@nagaranbasaran?utm_content=creditCopyText&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=unsplash) on [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/white-and-black-concrete-building-near-green-trees-during-daytime-wlpuNfpsHNs?utm_content=creditCopyText&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=unsplash))

In this article, I’m going to discuss exactly what makes a great developer website, GitHub portfolio, and LinkedIn profile. I’ll share what to avoid — things that are a waste of time, red flags for employers, or will raise the wrong kinds of questions about your professional experience.

If you’re starting from scratch — with just your resume and maybe a few portfolio projects for GitHub — it will take about a month to launch all 3 of these projects. Your website will take the most time. (If you’re not a frontend engineer — you might be able to skip a personal website entirely in favor of another portfolio project of your choice.) Your GitHub portfolio is going to be surprisingly easy, since there isn’t much you can add to your GitHub profile, and your LinkedIn profile will be almost exactly the same as your resume, except for a few tips that will help you stand out there.

## Why a Website Makes You a Memorable Candidate

Of course, if you’re a currently-employed developer with years of experience with a specialist tech stack — then a personal website is definitely not necessary, not even for very senior engineering positions!

So if a personal website is totally unnecessary, why do I strongly recommend you put one together, and now? The reason is because a great personal website can help you catch the eye of hiring managers and be more memorable. Humans are inherently gossipy (as my wife puts it), and who wouldn’t want to procrastinate for a few minutes from work by checking out the “personal” website of a developer candidate?

Compared to staring at resume PDFs and GitHub portfolios, looking at someone’s actual website is thrilling, and it’s a project you have total control over. Additionally, a personal website can be a superb inclusion as part of your career programming portfolio, at least when it’s well executed. (If your design skills are especially bad, you may want to pay for a designer or buy something like [the Spotlight template from Tailwind](https://tailwindui.com/templates/spotlight).)

I’m a fresher web developer currently building my portfolio on GitHub, and I want to understand what recruiters and experienced developers look for the most.
I am trying to improve my GitHub profile so it looks more professional and helps me get better job opportunities in web development.
### What I am trying to do:
- Build a strong developer portfolio
- Showcase real-world projects
- Improve repository structure and documentation
- Make my profile attractive for recruiters and clients
### What I expected:
I expected that having multiple projects with good code and proper README files would be enough to create a strong impression.
### What happened instead:
I noticed that many developers have very well-structured profiles with pinned repositories, contribution activity, project demos, and professional documentation, and I’m not sure what matters the most.
### My Question:
Should freshers focus more on:
1. Project quantity
2. Project quality
3. Open-source contributions
4. Professional README and documentation
5. Live deployed projects
Which of these creates the strongest impact for recruiters?
I would love to hear advice from experienced developers and recruiters in the community.

## What matters
### 1.Project quality
If someone opens your code and gets confused in 30 seconds, they’ll just leave.
* * *
### 2\. README
This is underrated.

### 3\. Live demo
If your project is deployed, it changes everything.
People can see it instead of guessing how it works.
* * *
### 4.Pinned projects
Keep your best 3–5 projects at the top.
No one is going to search for your best work.
* * *
### 5\. Consistency

Just don’t disappear for months.
* * *

Nice to have, but not important in the beginning.

Most recruiters won’t spend more than a minute on your profile.
They just check:
- a few good projects
- clean code
- working demo
- clear explanation

Instead of starting new projects, fix your existing ones:
- clean your code
- improve UI
- write a better README
- deploy it

## Header
![README Header](https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=800%2Cheight=%2Cfit=scale-down%2Cgravity=auto%2Cformat=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fabj3vi39qtiihev6yr5x.png)

Add a hero image, or keep it simple like I did. I started with a simple headline "Hi there, I'm Julia" and placed a small GIF next to it because I love using GIFs and emojis, it's so me and that's what I want to show.

Then I started by introducing myself, who I am, what programming languages I use, and what I'm interested in. Use adjectives that best describe you.

## My Projects
![README section My Projects](https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=800%2Cheight=%2Cfit=scale-down%2Cgravity=auto%2Cformat=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2F3pf9dvi8t9w6o36oasi4.png)

I have received many compliments for this section, so I encourage you to showcase your projects as best you can.

You should fill in the **About** section completely to have as much information as possible about your project that the generator will use. There are many different colorful themes for your statistics.

![REPO Section About](https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=800%2Cheight=%2Cfit=scale-down%2Cgravity=auto%2Cformat=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fjdk59qpqliel4pjnc08i.png)

Just drag and drop it into edit mode and the video will be inserted.

## About Me
![README Section About Me](https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=800%2Cheight=%2Cfit=scale-down%2Cgravity=auto%2Cformat=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fgq6pu85f7y76qf4669w9.png)

If anyone has made it to this section, they are already interested.

I've written about my latest achievement, what I'm working on, and how I visualize the tools I work with (which I've also added to the header).

## Footer
![README Footer, Stats and Blog Articles](https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=800%2Cheight=%2Cfit=scale-down%2Cgravity=auto%2Cformat=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fa03k7hsk7kb0jbddh9ho.png)

At the bottom of my profile, I've added statistics about my time on GitHub and the programming languages I use most often.

I've also added links to my latest blog articles.

## In general
If you want to see the code of my README, you can easily view it like any other code on GitHub by clicking on the [pencil icon](https://github.com/YuriDevAT/YuriDevAT) in the upper right corner.

There is so much more you can add to your profile, like different fonts, styling, etc. Just google it (e.g. Awesome GitHub README profiles) and get inspired by these great READMEs.

![Thank you](https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=800%2Cheight=%2Cfit=scale-down%2Cgravity=auto%2Cformat=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdocs.google.com%2Fuc%3Fexport%3Ddownload%26id%3D166Ecq6uBl61U14OUlkHOHIBv2ArKoumJ)

_Thanks for your reading and time._ _I really appreciate it!_

GitHub Profile - YouTube Tap to unmute [GitHub Profile](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A09Axj8A8F0) [Julia Undeutsch](https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCTIGfoGC_sGTj1TIVwJ73iQ) Julia Undeutsch102 subscribers [Watch on](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A09Axj8A8F0) Nowadays, junior developers are wondering if a personal portfolio is still necessary to showcase their skills. On one hand, I would say yes, because recruiters don't always have a technical background and don't know what GitHub is about and how it works. So a typical website portfolio would still be the safe way to show everything about you. **But**, I really struggled with my portfolio for a long time: how should it look, how should I present myself and my projects, what colors should I even use? That was the moment when I thought, if I'm going to struggle with my personal website, I at least want to have something to show in case recruiters take notice of me. So I pimped out my GitHub profile, and guess what? In interviews, interviewers said they really liked my GitHub profile and saw that I had put a lot of time and effort into making it that good. They never mentioned my personal website. So if you're in the same situation as I was a few months ago and struggling with your personal website, you can at least create a nice GitHub profile to have something to show for it. ## Header ![README Header](https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=800%2Cheight=%2Cfit=scale-down%2Cgravity=auto%2Cformat=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fabj3vi39qtiihev6yr5x.png) Add a hero image, or keep it simple like I did. I started with a simple headline "Hi there, I'm Julia" and placed a small GIF next to it because I love using GIFs and emojis, it's so me and that's what I want to show. Under the heading, I added badges that lead to all my social media accounts that I created with [shield.io](https://shields.io/). Shields offers more than just social media badges, like GitHub stats, language badges, and more. Then I started by introducing myself, who I am, what programming languages I use, and what I'm interested in. This section should be short and include all the important information about you, such as area of expertise (front-end, back-end, AI, etc.), experience, and languages. Use adjectives that best describe you. ## My Projects ![README section My Projects](https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=800%2Cheight=%2Cfit=scale-down%2Cgravity=auto%2Cformat=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2F3pf9dvi8t9w6o36oasi4.png) I have received many compliments for this section, so I encourage you to showcase your projects as best you can. I have created a thumbnail for all my projects and included it above the stats that are automatically generated with [readme-stats](https://github.com/anuraghazra/github-readme-stats). The text is taken from the description in your repository in the **About** section on the right (in the description you should write what the project is about and what languages you used). You should fill in the **About** section completely to have as much information as possible about your project that the generator will use. There are many different colorful themes for your statistics. ![REPO Section About](https://media2.dev.to/dynamic/image/width=800%2Cheight=%2Cfit=scale-down%2Cgravity=auto%2Cformat=auto/https%3A%2F%2Fdev-to-uploads.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fuploads%2Farticles%2Fjdk59qpqliel4pjnc08i.png) Images can be inserted by adding the URL of the image. ### [Underdog.io / Blog](https://underdog.io/blog-jobseekers)

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/61f9a3b8fc4971c862c40013/67819c4c67d790b7d813b412_Let%20the%20underdog%20team%20do%20the%20heavy%20lifting.jpg)

# How to make your GitHub more impressive to Employers

By

[The Underdog.io Team](https://underdog.io/blog/how-to-make-your-github-more-impressive-to-employers#)

January 10, 2025

No items found.

Are you a developer looking to stand out in a crowded job market? Your GitHub profile might be the key to catching an employer's eye!

In today's hiring landscape, a well-curated GitHub can be your secret weapon. It's not just about the code you write; it's about how you present yourself and your projects. From pinning your best repositories to crafting an eye-catching profile README, there are countless ways to make your GitHub profile _shine_. But where do you start? And how do you ensure your profile truly reflects your skills and potential?

Let's dive into the **essential strategies** to elevate your GitHub game and impress potential employers. We'll cover everything from optimizing your profile layout to showcasing your coding frequency, and even touch on related topics like coding interviews and the bootcamp vs. degree debate. By the end of this post, you'll have a clear roadmap to transform your GitHub into a powerful tool for career advancement.

‍

# Pin and Order Your Best Repositories

### Showcasing Your Best Work

When it comes to making your GitHub profile stand out to potential employers, pinning and ordering your best repositories is a crucial first step. This simple yet effective strategy allows you to highlight your most impressive projects and skills right at the top of your profile.

#### How to Pin Repositories

1. Navigate to your GitHub profile
2. Click on "Customize your pins"
3. Select up to six repositories to pin
4. Drag and drop to reorder them

#### Choosing What to Pin

When selecting repositories to pin, consider the following factors:

- Relevance to your target job or industry
- Complexity and scope of the project
- Code quality and documentation
- Recent activity or updates

#### Ordering Strategy

Arrange your pinned repositories in a way that tells a story about your skills and progression. Consider placing your most impressive or relevant project first, followed by others that complement or expand on your expertise.

By carefully selecting and ordering your pinned repositories, you create a curated showcase of your best work, making it easy for potential employers to quickly assess your capabilities and interests. This strategic approach to repository management can significantly enhance your GitHub profile's impact and improve your visibility to recruiters and hiring managers in the tech industry.

# Give Yourself a Profile Picture, Username and Bio

### Profile Picture

Your GitHub profile picture is often the first impression employers will have of you. Choose a professional, high-quality image that represents you well. A clear headshot or a creative avatar that aligns with your personal brand can make a lasting impact.

### Username

Select a username that is professional and memorable. Ideally, it should be:

- Easy to spell and pronounce
- Related to your real name or professional identity
- Consistent across other professional platforms

### Bio

Craft a concise yet impactful bio that showcases your skills, experience, and interests. Your bio should:

- Highlight your expertise
- Mention your current role or aspirations
- Include relevant technologies you work with
- Showcase any notable achievements or contributions

Here's a comparison of effective and ineffective bios:

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/61f9a3b8fc4971c862c40013/67819d07ff9b9067e077be0a_6781916a57f74b39c8a97683_Effective%2520github%2520bio.jpeg)

Remember, your profile picture, username, and bio work together to create a cohesive professional image. Regularly update these elements to reflect your current skills and career goals. With these optimizations, you'll significantly enhance your GitHub profile's appeal to potential employers.

# Create an Amazing Readme for Each of the Projects You Have Pinned

### Why a Great README Matters

A well-crafted README is the gateway to your project, offering a crucial first impression to potential employers and collaborators. It serves as a comprehensive guide, providing essential information about your work and showcasing your ability to communicate technical concepts effectively.

#### Key Elements of an Impressive README

1. Project Title and Description
2. Technologies Used
3. Installation Instructions
4. Usage Examples
5. Features and Functionality
6. Screenshots or Demo
7. Contributing Guidelines
8. License Information

#### Structuring Your README

Here's a suggested structure for an impressive README:

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/61f9a3b8fc4971c862c40013/67819d07ff9b9067e077be11_6781921e78ce1382ebe26a03_READme%2520structure%2520github.jpeg)

#### Tips for README Excellence

- Use clear and concise language
- Include badges for build status, test coverage, etc.
- Provide links to live demos or deployed versions
- Keep it up-to-date with the latest project changes
- Use formatting (headers, lists, code blocks) for readability

By creating impressive READMEs for your pinned projects, you demonstrate attention to detail and professionalism, making your GitHub profile more appealing to potential employers.

# Add a Profile Readme

### Creating an Impressive Profile README

A profile README is a powerful tool to showcase your skills, projects, and personality on GitHub. It's the first thing visitors see when they land on your profile, making it crucial for creating a strong first impression.

#### How to Create a Profile README

1. Create a new repository with the same name as your GitHub username
2. Add a `README.md` file to this repository
3. GitHub will automatically display this README on your profile

#### Elements of an Effective Profile README

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/61f9a3b8fc4971c862c40013/67819d07ff9b9067e077be07_678192cb78ce1382ebe31455_Elements%2520of%2520an%2520effective%2520profile%2520readme%2520github.jpeg)

#### Tips for an Outstanding README

- Use markdown to format your README attractively
- Include badges to showcase your skills and certifications
- Add GIFs or images to make it visually appealing
- Keep it concise and easy to scan
- Update it regularly to reflect your latest work and skills

By creating a compelling profile README, you significantly enhance your GitHub presence, making it more attractive to potential employers. This personal touch can set you apart from other candidates and provide a quick overview of your capabilities and interests.

# If Your Heatmap is Bare, You Should be Coding More

### The Importance of a Vibrant GitHub Heatmap

Your GitHub heatmap is a visual representation of your coding activity, and it's one of the first things potential employers notice when they visit your profile. A bare heatmap can send the wrong message, suggesting a lack of consistency or dedication to coding. Here's why you should focus on filling up your heatmap and how to do it effectively:

#### Benefits of a Well-Populated Heatmap

- **Demonstrates Consistency**: Shows you code regularly
- **Showcases Dedication**: Indicates passion for programming
- **Attracts Attention**: Makes your profile stand out

#### Strategies to Enhance Your Heatmap

1. **Daily Coding Habit**: Commit to coding at least once a day
2. **Contribute to Open Source**: Participate in community projects
3. **Work on Personal Projects**: Develop and update your own repositories
4. **Code Challenges**: Solve programming problems on platforms like LeetCode or HackerRank

Remember, quality matters as much as quantity. While a populated heatmap is impressive, ensure your contributions are meaningful and showcase your skills effectively. Employers value consistent, high-quality work over superficial activity. By coding regularly and contributing meaningfully, you'll not only improve your heatmap but also enhance your skills and portfolio.

# Make your Embarrassing Repositories Private

### Cleaning Up Your GitHub Profile

When it comes to impressing potential employers with your GitHub profile, sometimes less is more. Private repositories can be a powerful tool for curating your professional image. Here's why and how you should make your less polished repositories private:

#### Why Hide Certain Repositories?

- **Quality Over Quantity**: Employers value high-quality work over a large number of mediocre projects.
- **Focus on Strengths**: Highlighting your best work allows employers to quickly see your capabilities.
- **Professional Image**: Removing unfinished or experimental projects maintains a polished profile.

#### How to Make Repositories Private

1. Navigate to the repository you want to hide
2. Click on "Settings"
3. Scroll down to the "Danger Zone"
4. Click "Change visibility"
5. Select "Make private"
6. Confirm the change

By carefully curating your public repositories, you're not just hiding work; you're strategically presenting your best self to potential employers. This focused approach can significantly enhance your GitHub profile's impact and improve your chances of landing that dream developer job.

Now that you've cleaned up your profile, let's explore how diversifying your project types can further impress potential employers.

# Diversifying Your GitHub Portfolio

#### Types of Projects to Showcase

To make your GitHub profile truly stand out, it's crucial to demonstrate a diverse range of skills and experiences. Here's a breakdown of the different types of projects you should consider:

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/61f9a3b8fc4971c862c40013/67819d07ff9b9067e077be0d_6781977a0326d1da5d31253f_Types%2520of%2520Projects%2520to%2520Showcase%2520Github.jpeg)

#### Balancing Your Portfolio

A well-rounded GitHub profile should include:

1. At least one substantial application project
2. Two or more libraries or tools
3. Multiple open source contributions, even if they're small

#### Strategies for Open Source Contributions

- Start with documentation improvements
- Fix small bugs or add minor features
- Contribute to projects you use regularly

By diversifying your GitHub portfolio, you demonstrate versatility and a broad skill set to potential employers. This approach not only showcases your technical abilities but also highlights your adaptability and willingness to engage with the wider developer community. Remember, quality matters more than quantity, so focus on creating meaningful contributions across different project types.

# Try to Get Some Stars

### Boost Your Repository's Visibility

To make your GitHub profile more impressive to potential employers, it's crucial to get stars on your repositories. Stars serve as a measure of popularity and quality, indicating that others find your projects valuable or interesting.

#### Strategies to Attract Stars

1. Create High-Quality Projects
   - Develop unique and innovative solutions
   - Ensure thorough documentation
   - Maintain clean, well-commented code
2. Promote Your Repositories
   - Share on social media platforms
   - Participate in coding forums and communities
   - Write blog posts about your projects
3. Collaborate with Others
   - Contribute to open-source projects
   - Engage in coding challenges and hackathons
   - Network with fellow developers

#### Impact of Stars on Your Profile

![](https://cdn.prod.website-files.com/61f9a3b8fc4971c862c40013/67819d07ff9b9067e077be01_678197e082dbbad90aa95bdc_Impact%2520of%2520Stars%2520on%2520Your%2520Github%2520Profile.jpeg)

Remember, quality always trumps quantity. Focus on creating meaningful projects that solve real problems or showcase your unique skills. Engage with the developer community, respond to issues, and continuously improve your repositories. As you build a reputation for producing valuable work, you'll naturally attract more stars and catch the eye of potential employers.

# Dedicate Some Time to Optimizing Your GitHub

Optimizing your GitHub profile is an ongoing process that requires dedication and regular attention. By investing time in this effort, you can significantly enhance your visibility to potential employers and showcase your skills more effectively.

#### Key areas to focus on:

- **Profile Maintenance**: Regularly update your profile information, including your bio, profile picture, and pinned repositories.
- **Project Updates**: Keep your repositories current by adding new features, fixing bugs, and improving documentation.
- **Contribution Consistency**: Aim for regular contributions to maintain an active GitHub presence.
- **Readme Refinement**: Continuously improve your profile and project readmes to better communicate your skills and project details.

Creating a habit of dedicating time to GitHub optimization will pay off in the long run. It not only keeps your profile fresh and engaging but also demonstrates to potential employers your commitment to continuous improvement and your ability to manage and showcase your work effectively.

Now that we've covered the importance of dedicating time to optimizing your GitHub, let's explore some additional strategies to make your profile stand out even more.

# Conclusion

Your GitHub profile is your digital resume in the tech world. By implementing these strategies, you can transform it into a powerful showcase of your skills and projects. From pinning your best repositories to crafting engaging READMEs, each step contributes to a more impressive and professional GitHub presence.

Remember, optimizing your GitHub is an ongoing process. Regularly update your profile, contribute to open-source projects, and continue building diverse applications. With a well-curated GitHub, you'll not only catch the eye of potential employers but also demonstrate your commitment to continuous learning and growth in the field of software development.
